title: Because of the criticism, I started limiting the AI in my game
author: Forward_Key_4937
selftext: Hey. As you know, I'm making a game called Arkansas 2125 and I've always bragged about using AI and I enjoy doing it because it helps with the coding and creates nice graphics and textures. I then refine the textures to make them more human-like. And here's the problem: many people criticize the minimal use of any AI. Why did I start limiting them? At the beginning I made capsule graphics without AI completely. Yesterday I released an update where all the backgrounds in the prologue and endings are AI-free. The menu no longer has any AI, for example, My game already looks 100% human-made visually. But I still don't want to give up on upscaling, item label generation, and poster generation via chat gpt or Gemini.People do so much to make the game more qualitative, they try for hours and still some guy comes and sees the inscription that they are generated by AI and writes no thank you. I have to mark it on Steam because otherwise players will report me, so I'm adding a note that I only use it for some textures and language translations. Despite this, there are people who, after seeing only the note about AI, immediately do not want to play instead of giving it a chance, and the game is not expensive, only $5. Why, despite my best efforts, my game seems to be placed in line with games where AI is used everywhere. Is it so hard to accept there is a bit of AI but it is not visible at first glance so I will play.When will people finally accept that having a few textures isn't a sin, and that it saves time and money even in solo game development? What do you think?
